slides.title: Real Analysis

slides.html:
Where Does the Riemann Integral Fall Short?

  1. Limits and integrals do not commute: \chi_{\mathbb Q} is a limit of Riemann integrable functions but is not integrable itself
  2. Function spaces are incomplete: Cauchy sequences of continuous functions may have no limit
  3. Complicated sets cannot be measured: needed in probability and Fourier analysis

Lebesgue's idea: partition the range

\int f\approx\sum_iy_i\cdot m\{y_{i-1}<f\le y_i\}

The price: first define the "size" of irregular sets — measure theory
slides.title: Where Does the Riemann Integral Fall Short?

slides.html:
1. The Size of Sets: Cardinality

"Countable" is the dividing line between finite and the continuum
slides.title: 1. The Size of Sets: Cardinality

slides.html:
Equipotence and Countability

  • A\sim B: a bijection exists; Schröder–Bernstein: injections both ways ⟹ equipotent
  • Countable: injects into \mathbb N; countable unions of countable sets are countable
  • \mathbb Z,\mathbb Q countable; \mathbb R\sim[0,1]\sim[0,1]^2\sim2^{\mathbb N}
  • Cantor's theorem: X<2^X, via A=\{x:x\notin f(x)\}

Dimension does not change cardinality: \mathbb R^n\sim\mathbb R; but the power set is strictly bigger.
slides.title: Equipotence and Countability

slides.html:
2. Lebesgue Measure

Volume for as many sets as possible: not all sets, but all measurable ones
slides.title: 2. Lebesgue Measure

slides.html:
Measurable Sets (Carathéodory)

E\text{ measurable}\iff m^*(F)=m^*(F\cap E)+m^*(F\cap E^c)\quad\forall F
  • Measurable sets form a σ-algebra; the measure is countably additive
  • Null sets, boxes, open, closed, G_\delta, F_\sigma sets are measurable
  • Measurable = Borel minus null
  • Continuity: increasing m(\bigcup E_j)=\lim m(E_j); decreasing needs m(E_1)<\infty

Borel–Cantelli: \sum m(E_k)<\infty\Rightarrow almost every point is in only finitely many E_k.
slides.title: Measurable Sets (Carathéodory)

slides.html:
A Non-Measurable Set: Vitali

  • x\sim y\iff x-y\in\mathbb Q; choose one representative per class to get E
  • [0,1)=\bigsqcup_{q\in\mathbb Q}(E+q\bmod1), countably many disjoint translates
1=\sum_{q}m(E)\in\{0,\infty\}\quad\text{contradiction}

No translation-invariant, countably additive volume exists on all sets — measures live on σ-algebras.
slides.title: A Non-Measurable Set: Vitali

slides.html:
3. Measurable Functions

Functions with measurable level sets; closed under limits
slides.title: 3. Measurable Functions

slides.html:
Measurable Functions

  • f measurable ⟺ \{f\le a\} measurable ⟺ preimages of open (Borel) sets measurable
  • f\ge0 measurable ⟺ the region \{0\le y\le f(x)\} is measurable

Closure:

\{f+g<a\}=\bigcup_{q\in\mathbb Q}\{f<q\}\cap\{g<a-q\}
  • cf, f+g, fg, g\circ f (g continuous)
  • \sup f_n, \inf f_n, \limsup, \liminf, limits

Contrast: pointwise limits of continuous functions can be discontinuous; limits of measurable functions stay measurable.
slides.title: Measurable Functions

slides.html:
4. The Lebesgue Integral

Indicators → simple functions → non-negative functions → general functions
slides.title: 4. The Lebesgue Integral

slides.html:
The Three Convergence Theorems

Theorem Hypothesis Conclusion
Monotone (Levi) 0\le f_j\uparrow f \int f_j\to\int f
Fatou f_j\ge0 \int\liminf f_j\le\liminf\int f_j
Dominated (DCT) f_j\to f a.e., $ f_j
\text{Proof of DCT: Fatou on }g\pm f_j\ge0,\text{ then cancel }\int g
  • Corollary: non-negative series can be integrated term by term
  • Absolute continuity: m(E)<\delta\Rightarrow\int_E|f|<\varepsilon
slides.title: The Three Convergence Theorems

slides.html:
Riemann ⊂ Lebesgue

Theorem: Riemann integrable ⟹ Lebesgue integrable, with the same integral

  • Upper and lower step functions on dyadic partitions: m_n\le f\le M_n
  • \int M_n,\int m_n are the Darboux sums
  • DCT ⟹ \int M=\int m ⟹ M=m=f a.e.
slides.title: Riemann ⊂ Lebesgue

slides.html:
5. Modes of Convergence

Value at each point, size of the bad set, total integral of the error
slides.title: 5. Modes of Convergence

slides.html:
Littlewood's Three Principles

Principle Theorem
Measurable sets are nearly finite unions of intervals Borel approximation
Measurable functions are nearly continuous Luzin
Convergent sequences are nearly uniformly convergent Egorov

After removing an arbitrarily small set, the objects of measure theory behave like those of classical analysis.
slides.title: Littlewood's Three Principles

slides.html:
6. Lᵖ Spaces

Complete function spaces; orthogonal projections in L²
slides.title: 6. Lᵖ Spaces

slides.html:
Hölder and Minkowski

ab\le\frac{a^p}p+\frac{b^q}q\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\int|fg|\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q
\|f+g\|_p\le\|f\|_p+\|g\|_p
  • On finite measure spaces: L^1\supseteq L^p\supseteq L^{p'}\supseteq L^\infty (p<p')
  • \int|f|^p\le m(E)^{1-p/p'}\big(\int|f|^{p'}\big)^{p/p'}
slides.title: Hölder and Minkowski

slides.html:
Completeness: Riesz–Fischer

  1. Subsequence with \|f_{j_{k+1}}-f_{j_k}\|<2^{-k}
  2. F=|f_{j_1}|+\sum|f_{j_{k+1}}-f_{j_k}|, MCT ⟹ \int F<\infty
  3. The series converges absolutely a.e.; call the sum f
  4. Fatou ⟹ the subsequence converges in L^p
  5. Cauchy + convergent subsequence ⟹ the whole sequence converges

Exactly what Riemann integration could not do: L^p has no holes.
slides.title: Completeness: Riesz–Fischer

slides.html:
7. Fubini's Theorem

Slice, integrate, integrate again
slides.title: 7. Fubini's Theorem

slides.html:
Structure of the Proof

boxes → finite unions → countable unions (MCT) → null sets → bounded measurable sets → all sets

indicators → simple functions → non-negative functions (MCT twice) → integrable functions

Without integrability both iterated integrals may exist and differ: check \int|f|<\infty with Tonelli first.
slides.title: Structure of the Proof

slides.html:
8. Abstract Measures

Measure theory is the language of probability
slides.title: 8. Abstract Measures

slides.html:
Algebras, σ-Algebras and Extension

  • Algebra: closed under complements and finite intersections; σ-algebra: countable intersections
  • \mathcal A(\mathcal E): complements, then finite intersections, then finite unions; \sigma(\mathcal E) has no explicit form
  • Borel σ-algebra: generated by (a,b] or by open sets

Carathéodory extension: a measure on an algebra ⟹ a measure on \sigma(\mathcal A) (unique if σ-finite)

outer measure → Carathéodory measurable sets → σ-algebra → measure
slides.title: Algebras, σ-Algebras and Extension

slides.html:
Lebesgue–Stieltjes Measures

f increasing, right-continuous: \mu_f((a,b])=f(b)-f(a)

  • Right-continuity ⟺ countable additivity (compactness + enlarged open cover)
  • Every locally finite Borel measure on \mathbb R is some \mu_f
  • f=x: Lebesgue; f=\chi_{[a,\infty)}: Dirac; f=\int\alpha: density
  • Counting measure: \int g\,d\mu=\sum g(n) ⟹ non-negative double series can be reordered
slides.title: Lebesgue–Stieltjes Measures
The Cantor Function and Singular Measures

9. Differentiation and Integration

When does the fundamental theorem hold? Exactly for absolutely continuous functions
slides.title: 9. Differentiation and Integration

slides.html:
Integrate, Then Differentiate

Lebesgue differentiation: F=\int_a^xf ⟹ F'=f a.e.

  • Tool: the Vitali covering lemma
  • E_{p,q}=\{\overline DF>q>p>f\} ⟹ q\,m(E_{p,q})\le p\,m(E_{p,q})+\varepsilon
  • Applications: approximate identities n\varphi(nx), the heat kernel u(t,x)\to f(x)
slides.title: Integrate, Then Differentiate

slides.html:
Differentiate, Then Integrate

Class f' \int_a^bf'
Monotone exists a.e. \le f(b)-f(a)
Bounded variation = increasing − increasing exists a.e. may differ
Absolutely continuous exists a.e., integrable =f(b)-f(a)
  • Absolutely continuous: \sum(b_j-a_j)<\delta\Rightarrow\sum|f(b_j)-f(a_j)|<\varepsilon
  • f is an indefinite integral ⟺ f is absolutely continuous
  • The Cantor function: continuous, BV, but not absolutely continuous
slides.title: Differentiate, Then Integrate

slides.html:
The Radon–Nikodym Theorem

\nu\ll\mu\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\nu(E)=\int_E\frac{d\nu}{d\mu}\,d\mu
  • \nu\ll\mu: \mu(E)=0\Rightarrow\nu(E)=0
  • On \mathbb R: \mu_f\ll m\iff f absolutely continuous, density =f'
  • Probability: densities, conditional expectation, likelihood ratios, change of measure
slides.title: The Radon–Nikodym Theorem
